findings.title: Public conversation pages still fetch unbounded message histories
findings.rationale: PublicConversationsController.conversations loads multiple parent conversations with include.messages ordered by createdAt/id and take: 1. With the supplied Prisma 6 configuration, which does not enable relationJoins, multi-parent nested pagination uses the query loading strategy and applies the per-parent limit in memory; the child query can retrieve every matching message for those conversations. A page containing a long-history conversation therefore has unbounded database transfer and application hydration despite the 500-parent cap. The supplied EPS counters measure binding, credential and latest-IN queries, while the 500-reference EXPLAIN measures the separate window projection; neither measures this initial child fetch. This is a concrete resource-exhaustion path in the touched public listing and conflicts with D07/SCOPE-06's bounded-read premise. The approved managed latest-IN index does not resolve this separate hydration behavior.
findings.suggested_action: Retrieve latest-message fields through a database-bounded batched top-one-per-conversation query, preserving ordering, response fields and lookahead semantics. Avoid per-conversation application queries. Capture the actual endpoint SQL and execution work with multiple parents and a deep message history, proving that child retrieval stays bounded by the page rather than total history; then run fresh canonical validation.

findings.title: Repeated limit parameters now produce an uncaught type error
findings.rationale: limitePublico calls valor.trim() before checking its runtime type. Express represents repeated query parameters such as limit=17&limit=18 as an array, regardless of the Record<string, string> annotation. Both touched GET endpoints consequently return HTTP 500 for that input. The previous Number-based expression fell back to the default for this repeated-value case. This remains bounded and is non-blocking compatibility debt, not a severe performance exposure.
findings.suggested_action: Accept unknown input at the normalization boundary and handle non-string values explicitly, preferably using the existing default behavior. Add request-level coverage for repeated values on both endpoints.
